questions.q: A cubical solid aluminum <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>bulk</mi><mo> </mo><mi>modulus</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>V</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>P</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi>V</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn><mo> </mo><mi>GPa</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> block has an edge length of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> on the surface of the earth. It is kept on the floor of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi></math> deep ocean. Taking the average density of water and the acceleration due to gravity to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively, the change in the edge length of the block in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>mm</mi></math> is ________.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A steel wire of diameter <math><mn>0.5</mn><mi>m</mi><mi>m</mi></math> and Young's modulus <math><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>11</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi>N</mi><msup><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> carries a load of mass M. The length of the wire with the load is 1.0 m. A vernier scale with 10 divisions is attached to the end of this wire. Next to the steel wire is a reference wire to which a main scale, of least count 1.0 mm, is attached. The 10 divisions of the vernier scale correspond to 9 divisions of the main scale. Initially, the zero of vernier scale coincides with the zero of main scale. If the load on the steel wire is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1.2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>k</mi><mi>g</mi></math> , the vernier scale division which coincides with a main scale division is __________. Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><mi>m</mi><msup><mi>s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><mo>=</mo><mi> </mi><mn>3.2</mn><mi> </mi><mo>.</mo></math>
questions.solution:
d=0.5 mm
Y=2×1011
l=1m
∆l=FlAy=mglπd24y=1.2×10×1π4×5×10-42×2×1011
∆l=1.2×103.24×25×10-8×2×1011
= 121.6×25×103=1240×103=0.03mm
So 3rd division of vernier scale will coincicle with main scale

questions.q: In plotting stress versus strain curves for two materials P and Q , a student by mistake puts strain on the y -axis and stress on the x - axis as shown in the figure. Then the correct statement(s) is(are)
options: The Young's modulus of  <math><mi>P</mi></math>  is more than that of  <math><mi>Q</mi></math>
questions.solution:
Slope of this graph represents the reciprocal of Young's modulus.
Since slope of P>  slope of Q
Hence Y of P<Y of Q

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One end of a horizontal thick copper wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><mo> </mo></math>and radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> is welded to an end of another horizontal thin copper wire of length<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> and radius<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math>. When the arrangement stretched by applying forces at two ends, the ratio of the elongation in the thin wire to that in the thick wire is
questions.solution:
As the two rods are in series, the force at the connecting surface will be same.

F1=F2

⇒Y×∆l1l1×A1=Y×∆l2l2×A2

Where Y is Young's modulus, ∆l1 and ∆l2 is increase in length, l1 and l2 are lengths, A1 and A2 are areas, 2R and R are radii of thick and thin wires respectively.

∵ F=Y×strain×Area

⇒∆l1l1×A1=∆l2l2×A2

Here, A1=π2R2, l1=2L

A2=πR2, l2=L
⇒ ∆l12L×π2R2=∆l2L×πR2
⇒ ∆l2∆l1=2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $0.1 \mathrm{~kg}$ mass is suspended from a wire of negligible mass. The length of the wire is $1 \mathrm{~m}$ and its cross-sectional area is $4.9 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m}^2$. If the mass is pulled a little in the vertically downward direction and released, it performs simple harmonic motion of angular frequency $140 \mathrm{rad} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$. If the Young's modulus of the material of the wire is $n \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$, the value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
$\omega=\sqrt{\frac{K}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{Y A}{l m}}=\sqrt{\frac{\left(n \times 10^9\right)\left(4.9 \times 10^{-7}\right)}{1 \times 0.1}}$
Putting, $\omega=140 \operatorname{rad} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ in above equation we get,

n=4

$\therefore$ Answer is 4 .
